## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `Examples`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `twilio-example`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **Examples**.

## Step 2: Open the add connection panel

1. Select **Add Connection** (the `+` icon next to **Connections**) in the WSO2 Integrator panel to open the connector palette.

## Step 3: Select the Twilio connector

1. Search for "twilio" in the palette, then select **Twilio** from the search results to open the **Configure Twilio** form.

## Step 4: Fill in connection parameters

1. <!-- manual: Enter the connection parameters, binding each to a configurable variable to keep credentials out of source code: - accountSid : Twilio Account SID, bound to a string configurable variable - authToken : Twilio Auth Token, bound to a string configurable variable - connectionName : Name for this connection instance (for example, twilioClient) -->

## Step 5: Save the connection

1. Select **Save Connection** to persist the connection.

## Step 6: Set actual values for your configurables

1. In the left panel, select **Configurations** to open the Configurations panel.
2. Run the shell command `.venv/bin/python tools/write_config.py --project twilio-example --expect accountSid,authToken` to set the configurable values.

## Step 7: Add an automation entry point

1. In the integration overview, select **+ Add Artifact**, then select **Automation** from the artifact type list, and select **Create**.

## Step 8: Select and configure the createMessage operation

1. In the Automation flow editor, select **+** button between **Start** and **Error Handler** to open the node panel.
2. Select **twilioClient**.
3. Select **Create Message** from the **Message** group to open the **twilioClient → createMessage** configuration form.
4. Enter the following values in the **Payload** field: - **To** : Recipient phone number in E.164 format - **From** : Your Twilio-provisioned sender number - **Body** : The SMS message text - **Result** : Auto-named result variable (`twilioMessage`) of type `twilio:Message` Select **Save**.
5. <!-- manual: Enter the following values in the Payload field: - To : Recipient phone number in E.164 format - From : Your Twilio-provisioned sender number - Body : The SMS message text - Result : Auto-named result variable (twilioMessage) of type twilio:Message Select Save. -->

## Step 9: Open the Artifacts palette

1. Select **Add Artifact** in the WSO2 Integrator panel to open the Artifacts palette.
2. <!-- manual: Scroll to the Event Integration category and locate the Twilio card. -->

## Step 10: Fill in the trigger configuration form

1. Select **Twilio** card to open the trigger configuration form, then configure the listener parameters: - **Service Type**: The service type for this trigger: `SmsStatusService` is pre-selected - **Webhook Listener Port**: The port on which the Twilio webhook listener accepts incoming HTTP status callbacks from Twilio: bind this field to a `configurable int` variable named `listenerPort`.
2. <!-- manual: configure the listener parameters -->

## Step 11: Set actual values for your configurations

1. Select **Configurations** in the left panel of WSO2 Integrator.
2. <!-- manual: Set a value for each configuration listed below: - listenerPort (int) : The port on which the Twilio webhook listener will accept incoming HTTP status callbacks from Twilio -->

## Step 12: Create the trigger

1. Select **Create** to generate the integration.

## Step 13: Inspect the pre-registered event handlers

1. Select **twilio:SmsStatusService** in the left project tree to open the Twilio Event Integration service view. > **Note:** Unlike Kafka or RabbitMQ, the Twilio `SmsStatusService` pre-registers all nine SMS status handlers at service creation time.

## Step 14: Open the onReceived handler flow

1. Select **onReceived** row to navigate to its flow canvas. > **Note:** The `onReceived` handler uses the library-defined `twilio:SmsStatusChangeEventWrapper` payload type.

## Step 15: Add a log step

1. Select **+** icon in the flow chart.
2. In the side panel that opens, select **Log Info** from the **Logging** section.
3. <!-- manual: enter event.toJsonString() as the message -->
